6. RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN LOCAL SHORT-TERM USES OF MAN'S ENVIRONMENT AND THE MAINTENANCE AND ENHANCEMENT OF LONG-TERM PRODUCTIVITY
Short-term uses of the environment as considered in this statement refer to those associated with a license period of up to 50 years, as opposed to long-term productivity which would refer to a much greater time period. Long-term productivity would refer to all aspects of the environment which would, on a long-term basis, be affected by the project.
6.1 SHORT-TERM USES
The short-term uses of the local environment would provide benefits in power generation, economic growth, and to a limited extent, recreational use. Construction and operation of the project would result in several ecological alterations to the area.
Sections of free-flowing stream within the project boundary would be eliminated and replaced by a reservoir that, with appurtenant structures, would eliminate about 505 acres of land, with attendant losses of wildlife and their habitat as well as other uses. Activities such as construction of the project works and clearing the construction yard would cause short-term adverse effects on fish and wildlife populations in or adjacent to the proposed project area, as described in Subsections 3.1.2 and 3.2.2. Such effects would diminish the full range of existing beneficial uses of these natural resources. Any benefits for wildlife species due to forest openings resulting from clearing the construction yard area would be a short-term enhancement.
Short-term benefits from the project during its period of operation include the generation of considerable peaking power to meet a growing consumer demand for electric energy, enlarged tax revenues from project works and real estate for immediate local-government use, and limited job opportunities provided by plant construction, maintenance, and operation. Any provisions for enlarged recreational use and improved sport fishery resources in the area would also be short-term enhancements.
